# Credentials

An `EmailAccount` authenticates one of two ways, distinguished by the `authType` enum
(`password` | `oauth`). Both secrets are stored encrypted; nothing else in the schema is.

## Encryption at rest

`common/crypto.util.ts` is thirty lines and everything else depends on its exact format.
[`encrypt()`](mex://function:6f128ba807f90fc18a5ba4cdc9abfd21) produces `aes-256-gcm` output serialized as three
base64 fields joined by colons — `iv:ciphertext:authTag` — with a random 12-byte IV per call.
[`decrypt()`](mex://function:d830577584e686a9b573dbb1eb2730a7) rejects anything that does not split into exactly three
parts, then verifies the GCM auth tag.

The key is `sha256(ENCRYPTION_KEY)`, so the env var may be any non-empty string; there is no
salt and no KDF iteration count. Consequences worth knowing before changing anything here:

- **`ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not rotatable in place.** Changing it makes every `encryptedPassword`
  and `encryptedRefreshToken` undecryptable, surfacing as GCM auth-tag failures on the next sync.
- Any new secret column must use the same helper, and any format change breaks existing rows.

## The single credential entry point

[`getImapCredentials()`](mex://method:8db2ea988568d42a5a28549ab3b32bf3) is the only
place that decrypts. It returns a discriminated union — `{ kind: "password", password }` or
`{ kind: "oauth", accessToken }` — and both IMAP callers branch on `credentials.kind` when
building their auth object. Never decrypt inline anywhere else.

For a `password` account it simply decrypts `encryptedPassword` (rejecting an account that has
none). For an `oauth` account it decrypts the refresh token, mints a fresh access token, and —
importantly — **persists a rotated refresh token if Google returns a new one** via
`updateRefreshToken`. Dropping that write silently breaks the account the next time Google
rotates.

## Google XOAUTH2

Scopes are `['https://mail.google.com/', 'email']`; the flow uses `access_type: 'offline'` and
`prompt: 'consent'` so a refresh token is always issued. It is entirely optional — with no
`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` the app boots and password accounts work normally.

The connect flow:

1. `POST /email-accounts/oauth/google/start` — `createAuthUrl` mints a random 16-byte `state`
   and stores the payload (`label`, or `accountId` when re-authorizing an existing account) in
   an **in-memory `Map` with a 10-minute TTL**. This state is lost on restart, so a connect
   flow cannot survive an API restart or be completed against a different process.
2. The user consents at Google and is redirected to the callback.
3. `consumeState` deletes and validates the state, then `exchangeCode` swaps the code for
   tokens. It throws if Google returns no refresh token — which happens when the app already
   holds a grant; the fix is to revoke access in the Google account settings and retry.
4. The encrypted refresh token is written to the account.

The redirect URI must match what is registered in GCP **exactly**, and a consent screen left in
"Testing" status expires refresh tokens after 7 days.

## The revocation loop

[`mintAccessToken()`](mex://method:0681ef04d931d5c8ff39d97649b54cca) calls
`refreshAccessToken()` and translates Google's `invalid_grant` into a typed `OAuthRevokedError`.
`getImapCredentials` catches only that type, sets `needsReauth: true` on the account, and
rethrows as a `BadRequestException` naming the re-connect endpoint. Any other error propagates
untouched.

Both `EmailSyncService.syncAccount` and `ImapIngestionService.ingestAccount` check
`account.needsReauth` **before** doing any work and refuse with a message pointing at
`POST /email-accounts/oauth/google/start`. So a revoked Gmail account fails fast and stays
failed until a human re-consents — it never silently degrades. Clearing the flag without a
successful re-consent just reproduces the failure one layer deeper.

## Handling rules

- Never log, return, or embed a decrypted password or access token. `toResponse()` is the
  account serializer and it omits both encrypted columns.
- Resolve credentials as late as possible, immediately before constructing the IMAP client;
  access tokens are short-lived.
- `ENCRYPTION_KEY` lives in `.env`, which is gitignored (`.env.*` with `!.env.example`).
  There is also an `apps/api/.env` read when the process starts from that directory — keep
  both consistent.
